entries.claim: Skipping every existing fingerprint in either FILED.md state prevents an ambiguous create from being marked unconfirmed when a confirmed row already exists, contradicting D-06 and TRK-02.
entries.failure_scenario: A confirmed FILED.md row is one of the accepted orphaned rows, so a complete tracker miss correctly permits a new create. If that create lands but returns nonzero, mirrorFiled finds the existing confirmed fingerprint and skips the requested unconfirmed write. A retry during search-index lag sees another complete miss, treats the row as confirmed, and creates the same issue again.

entries.claim: The plan makes lookup availability global across all chunks, discarding usable answers when only one chunk fails.
entries.failure_scenario: With seven accepts, the first chunk completes and reports that one fingerprint already exists, while the second lookup exits nonzero. Because not every chunk completed, the plan marks the lookup unavailable; the successful hit is no longer authoritative, and without a FILED.md row that fingerprint is created again.

entries.claim: Giving an unconfirmed row precedence over every complete tracker answer contradicts D-04 and fails AC4's requirement to report the existing issue.
entries.failure_scenario: An ambiguous create lands and writes an unconfirmed row. On retry, the tracker has indexed the issue and returns a complete hit with number 42. Task 6 suppresses on the row “whatever the tracker answered” and reports only the row date and FILED.md, so the envelope omits issue 42 even though AC4 requires reporting the issue that already exists.

entries.claim: Refusing on an unreadable FILED.md before attempting the lookup contradicts D-04's locked rule that FILED.md is only a fallback when the tracker lookup could not run.
entries.failure_scenario: FILED.md is unreadable, but the forge is available and would return a complete answer. The planned reader refuses before spawning the lookup, so a ledger that should be irrelevant on a complete tracker path prevents the fire from proceeding.

entries.claim: The plan knowingly leaves the Forgejo and GitLab lookup semantics unproved even though failure of the assumption removes duplicate protection entirely on those providers.
entries.failure_scenario: If either CLI interprets the space-joined fingerprints as an AND or phrase search, an issue title containing one payload fingerprint is omitted from the complete response. The seam treats that empty result as authoritative and creates a duplicate; all planned byte-vector tests still pass, exactly as the note acknowledges.

entries.claim: Task 2's preservation check is not falsifiable as written because git diff --stat cannot show whether deleted lines came from the normalizeDeclines test block.
entries.failure_scenario: An executor deletes or rewrites existing normalizeDeclines cases while adding enough other lines for the test file to pass. git diff --stat reports only aggregate insertion and deletion counts, so the stated verification cannot establish that the required block remained unmodified.
